artifacts.summary: Confirms all cited line anchors in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh/orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh still hold, settles the exact hoist boundary and branch shape for the mint, pins the DELIVERABLE 2 assertion's insertion point and parse method, confirms the Group 19 test-stub gap, and argues the required correction to Group 19 case 1's durable-counter assertion (necessary but insufficient, needs a companion in-memory-counter assertion).

memory_candidates.content: In orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, mt_json.dispatch_seq_counter is a single GLOBAL scalar shared across all tasks dispatched in one /orchestrate run (mt_get/mt_set with no --arg t), while its durable persistence in each task's own .orchestrator-loop-guard file's dispatch_seq_counter field is per-task. Any fix touching seq minting/replay must account for this split scope or risk reasoning about the wrong counter.

cycle_plan_dispatch_hash() in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh deliberately strips '^- dispatch_seq: [0-9]+$' and '^- dispatch_start_ts: [0-9]+$' lines before hashing a composed dispatch file (for the identical-dispatch convergence guard). Any new consistency check that needs to read a dispatch file's actual dispatch_seq value must grep the Identity block directly and must never reuse this hash helper, which is seq-blind by design.

A test assertion that checks only a durable/persisted-file value can remain green across both a buggy and a fixed implementation if the actual defect lives in an ephemeral/in-memory value that never gets flushed either way (e.g. orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's replay branch never calls --flush-seq in either the buggy or fixed version). Such an assertion is not wrong, but is insufficient on its own and needs a companion assertion on the in-memory state to actually discriminate pre-fix from post-fix behavior.
